questions.problem:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}}-Q\frac{∂g}{\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}}+R)\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $z=g(x,y),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(x,y)=⟨x,\,y,\,g(x,y)⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨2x-z,\,y-z,\,z+y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=4x-y$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $-1\le y\le 2.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,4u-v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 2\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,\,1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x-z,\,y-z,\,z+y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=4u-v} \\  & =⟨2u-(4u-v),\,v-(4u-v),\,4u-v+v⟩ \\  & =⟨-2u+v,\,-4u+2v,\,4u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-2u+v,\,-4u+2v,\,4u⟩\cdot ⟨-4,\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(-2u+v)\cdot (-4)+(-4u+2v)\cdot 1+4u\cdot 1 \\  & =8u-4v+-4u+2v+4u \\  & =8u-2v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨2x-z,\,y-z,\,z+y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(8u-2v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}(8u-2v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨{cos}^{2}⁡(xy),\,{cos}^{2}⁡(xy),\,1⟩,
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=\operatorname{tan}⁡(xy)$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $-x\le y\le 0.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡(xy))=\frac{y}{{cos}^{2}⁡(xy)} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{tan}⁡(xy))=\frac{x}{{cos}^{2}⁡(xy)}\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the flux of $F$ through $S$ is given by 

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨{cos}^{2}⁡(xy),\,{cos}^{2}⁡(xy),\,1⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨{cos}^{2}⁡(xy),\,{cos}^{2}⁡(xy),\,1⟩{|}_{z=\operatorname{tan}⁡(xy)} \\  & =⟨{{{cos}^{2}⁡(xy)}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{{cos}^{2}⁡(xy)}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{1}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨{cos}^{2}⁡(xy),\,{cos}^{2}⁡(xy),\,1⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-({cos}^{2}⁡(xy))\cdot (\frac{y}{{cos}^{2}⁡(xy)})-({cos}^{2}⁡(xy))\cdot (\frac{x}{{cos}^{2}⁡(xy)})+1)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-y-x+1)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-x}^{0}(-y-x+1)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}-xy+y]}_{y=-x}^{y=0}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-{x}^{2}+x)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+x)\,dx \\  & ={[-\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨x+y,\,y-x,\,z⟩,
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ for $-1\le x\le 1$ and $-1\le y\le 1.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})=2x \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})=2y\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the flux of $F$ through $S$ is given by 

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨x+y,\,y-x,\,z⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨x+y,\,y-x,\,z⟩{|}_{z=1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =⟨{{x+y}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{y-x}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨x+y,\,y-x,\,z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-(x+y)\cdot (2x)-(y-x)\cdot (2y)+1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-2{x}^{2}-2xy-2{y}^{2}+2xy+1+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{[y-{x}^{2}y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{y=-1}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[(1-{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{3})-(-1+{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3})]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(2-2{x}^{2}-\frac{2}{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[2x-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{2}{3}x]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(2-\frac{2}{3}-\frac{2}{3})-(-2+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
